entity_ranked_evidence.title: Modi Has Few Good Options to Quell India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protests - Bloomberg.com
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Modi Has Few Good Options to Quell India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protests. ## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AISubscribe. What started as a satirical online movement two months ago has turned into one of India’s biggest student protests in years, sparking scenes of violent clashes in New Delhi. And Prime Minister Narendra Modi has few good options to stop them. Launched in May by young organizers with little political experience, the Cockroach Janta Party managed to draw crowds of students, parents and professionals into the heart of India’s capital, where they jumped police barricades and faced tear gas and baton charges in an attempt to march to the parliament on Monday. They started by demanding the resignation of India’s education minister after a series of exam scandals, but frustrations quickly morphed into broader anger at Modi’s government. entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: * #### Johnson scores major win as House GOP advances Trump’s top election priority. Republican strategist Collin Reed and Fox News contributor Richard Fowler weigh in on the escalating midterm election battles as 'America's Newsroom' anchor Bill Hemmer breaks down the power rankings for the House and Senate. Several findings in the latest Fox News Poll show voters are unhappy and want major change, which bodes well for Democrats in November: President Donald Trump’s job approval remains near a record low, more Democrats are motivated to vote, Republicans join Democrats and independents in rating the economy negatively, and 4 in 10 voters want "dramatic" or "revolutionary" change. Plus, more view the GOP as tied to elites than the Democratic Party. More Democrats (68%) say they are extremely motivated to vote in November than Republicans (57%) by an 11-point margin. The 15-point gap reflects more Democrats and independents saying the GOP is tied to elites, yet even Republicans are equally likely to describe both parties as close to elites.

entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # RVNL Wins ₹359 Crore Railway Contract for Bihar Rail Doubling. Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd (RVNL) has emerged as the lowest bidder for a ₹358.97 crore rail doubling project in Bihar awarded by East Central Railway. Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd (RVNL) has been announced as the lowest bidder for a ₹358.97 crore engineering, procurement, and construction contract awarded by the East Central Railway. The project is focused on the doubling of a 41.04 km rail line between Kundawa Chainpur and Raxaul in Bihar, which is part of the broader Sitamarhi-Raxaul corridor. As an engineering and construction entity, the company’s revenue and profit growth depend significantly on its ability to execute these long-term projects within the stipulated timelines and budgets. One of the primary monitorables for shareholders is the pace of execution for the company’s large order book. While RVNL has a strong track record of project delivery, investors typically watch for quarterly updates on billing milestones to ensure that revenue recognition is proceeding as planned.
